text: Jim drew a package from his overcoat pocket and threw it upon the table. <break time="0.8s" /> Do not make any mistake, Dell, he said. <break time="0.8s" /> No haircut could make me like my girl any less. <break time="0.8s" /> But open that package, and you will see why I was so shocked. <break time="0.8s" /> White fingers quickly tore at the string and paper. <break time="0.8s" /> Inside lay the Combs, the set of combs that Della had admired for a long time in a shop window on Broadway. <break time="0.8s" /> They were beautiful combs, made of pure tortoise shell, with jeweled edges. <break time="0.8s" /> But the hair that should have worn them was gone. <break time="0.8s" /> Della hugged them to her chest and smiled through her tears. <break time="0.8s" /> My hair grows so fast, Jim. <break time="0.8s" /> Then she held out the chain to him eagerly upon her open palm. <break time="0.8s" /> Is it not lovely, Jim, Give me your watch. <break time="0.8s" /> I want to see how the chain looks on it. <break time="0.8s" /> Instead of obeying, Jim sat down on the couch, put his hands under the back of his head, and smiled. <break time="0.8s" /> Dell, said he, I sold the watch to get the money to buy your combs. <break time="0.8s" /> The magi, as you know, were wise men who brought gifts to the Baby in the manger. <break time="0.8s" /> Here I have told you the story of two foolish children who sacrificed for each other the greatest treasures of their house. <break time="0.8s" /> But of all who give gifts, these two were the wisest. <break time="0.8s" /> They are the magi.
